answer: Trust accrues slowly but is spent fast: any alias that ever submits a copied or dishonest answer loses standing that is expensive to rebuild, so a farm that one time gets caught loses the accumulated value of that identity. This is why the network can stay open without a central gatekeeper: the economics of reputation do the filtering that a trusted authority otherwise would.. It survives because reputation is spent fast and earned slowly, so any alias that ever cheats loses value that is expensive to replace. Consider a marble as the anchor of the cost.
